articles.title: Find your way around LoreVia
articles.summary: Use Home, project overviews, breadcrumbs, presets, and hidden-tool recovery without losing your place.
articles.permission_notes: Some project tools may still require owner or collaborator permission.
steps: Choose Home to return to your Library.
Inside a project, choose Project overview to return to that book's starting page.
Use More tools or command search when a tool is hidden by your current complexity setting.
Open Settings to change Focused, Standard, or Power mode and to restart onboarding.
warnings: A hidden tool is not deleted. Plan locks, permission limits, and processing blocks are separate states.

articles.title: Reading and Writing workspaces
articles.summary: Reading is for enjoying and reviewing a book; Writing is for editing, story intelligence, and sharing.
articles.plan_notes: Writing access may require an Author plan or an editing collaboration permission.
articles.permission_notes: A disabled Writing option explains the exact restriction; it is not hidden.
steps: Open the project overview.
Choose Reading workspace for chapters, recaps, notes, quotes, and spoiler-safe tools.
Choose Writing workspace for the manuscript editor, story bible, analysis, collaboration, and exports.
If a switch fails, LoreVia restores the workspace saved on the server and shows the reason.
warnings: Switching workspaces changes the navigation, but it does not alter or delete book content.

articles.title: Create, upload, and import projects
articles.summary: Choose between a full manuscript import, chapter-by-chapter upload, pasted chapter, or an editor-first project.
articles.plan_notes: Manuscript authoring features require eligible Writing access.
articles.permission_notes: Only owners and collaborators with manuscript editing permission can change text.
steps: From Home, create or open a project.
Use Import & Export for whole files and automatic chapter splitting.
Use Add chapter or the manuscript editor when you already know the exact chapter number.
Review detected chapter titles and numbers before starting analysis.
warnings: If chapter numbers repeat, resolve them before replacing existing chapters.

articles.title: Save and recover a chapter
articles.summary: LoreVia keeps a local draft first, saves one chapter at a time, and separates saving from story-memory processing.
articles.permission_notes: Collaborators need permission for the selected chapter.
steps: Keep the editor open; your text is retained locally before the server request.
If Waiting for connection appears, reconnect and choose Retry.
For a conflict, compare the server version with the local draft before choosing which copy to keep.
A successful save may show story-memory refresh as pending; this does not mean the chapter save failed.
warnings: Do not clear browser storage until a waiting offline draft has synced or been downloaded.

articles.title: Understand processing and reprocessing
articles.summary: Processing turns saved chapters into searchable story memory and can be retried without resaving the text.
articles.plan_notes: Allowances depend on the account plan and processed-word capacity.
articles.permission_notes: Only eligible project members can start reprocessing.
steps: Confirm the chapter says Saved to LoreVia.
Check the project processing status for queued, running, paused, or failed chapters.
Retry processing from the project or manuscript controls; you do not need to paste the chapter again.
If repeated retries fail, create a support case with the safe request ID.
warnings: Saving and AI processing are separate. A processing failure does not erase the saved chapter.

articles.title: Choose a story-bible or analysis tool
articles.summary: A plain-language directory for characters, relationships, timeline, plot threads, worldbuilding, analysis, search, recaps, and grounded questions.
articles.plan_notes: Some AI and authoring tools require Writing access.
articles.permission_notes: Results follow project permissions and processing readiness.
steps: Use Character Bible, Relationships, Timeline, Plot Threads, Foreshadowing, World Gaps, or Series Wiki to organize extracted story facts.
Use Story Advisor for revision decisions and Editorial Review or Voice Consistency for focused review passes.
Use Ask LoreVia for manuscript-grounded questions; use Ask Support only for questions about operating LoreVia.
Use Search Passages for exact evidence and Recaps for spoiler-aware summaries.
warnings: Support Assistant never receives or searches manuscript text. Ask LoreVia is the book-grounded assistant.

articles.title: Reading, notes, quotes, and spoiler safety
articles.summary: Resume reading, control spoiler boundaries, save bookmarks, keep notes and quotes, and search what you have read.
articles.plan_notes: Core reading is available to readers with book access.
articles.permission_notes: Private notes and reading progress belong to the signed-in reader.
steps: Choose Reading workspace and Continue reading.
Use the reader toolbar to change typography or return to the project overview.
Save notes, highlights, and your reading place as you go.
Keep spoiler-safe behavior enabled when you only want information through your current chapter.
warnings: Turning off a spoiler boundary can reveal information from later chapters.

articles.title: Sharing, collaboration, beta reading, and rights
articles.summary: Understand the difference between private projects, collaborators, beta readers, public sharing, exports, and book discussions.
articles.permission_notes: Only owners can change visibility and manage all collaborators.
steps: Use Collaborators for people helping inside the writing workspace.
Use Beta Reads and Beta Feedback for structured reader assignments and responses.
Use Visibility Center before public sharing.
Use Import & Export to create files; Book discussions refers to LoreVia's public book forum.
warnings: Inviting a collaborator, assigning a beta reader, and publishing publicly grant different access. Review the chosen role before sending.

articles.title: Plans, billing, privacy, and account help
articles.summary: Find plan limits, permissions, billing controls, privacy actions, data deletion, and account recovery.
articles.plan_notes: Pricing and account settings are available to every signed-in user.
articles.permission_notes: Sensitive account actions may require recent authentication.
steps: Open Pricing to compare plan capabilities and limits.
Open Settings for account, privacy, workspace, and recovery controls.
For an unrecognized charge or inaccessible account, contact support without sharing passwords, payment details, or access tokens.
warnings: LoreVia support will never ask for your password or full payment-card number.

articles.title: Service status and human support
articles.summary: Check a problem or create a redacted human-support case.
articles.permission_notes: Creating a support case always requires your confirmation.
steps: Retry once and note the safe error code or request ID.
Use Ask Support for a guided answer based on LoreVia documentation.
Create a support case only after reviewing the redacted summary.
warnings: Do not include private manuscript text, passwords, payment details, or access tokens in a support case.
